why: A is the conjunction (universe 0) of the project's four lemmas for (ii)=>(i): exists_small_nhds, exists_approx, exists_isScSmoothMap_urysohn and admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx. B is the text's quotient construction (W, Q, f, g, γ = ĝ/Σĝ) plus conclusion (i). The project's proof is different (Urysohn functions plus Mathlib's BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity), but A => B goes through: (i) is A's 4th conjunct (via V5_57's atlas glue). The construction comes from A's first two conjuncts: exists_small_nhds, applied inside an open U' with cl(U') ⊆ U_i, supplies cl(φ(W)) ⊆ O, which the text does not arrange; exists_approx with ε = 1/4 supplies ĝ. Mathlib supplies the refinement and Q = {f = 1}. Then Σĝ ≥ 3/4, and ĝ/Σĝ is sc-smooth (locally ĝ·σ(Σĝ) with σ smooth, σ = 1/t on [c,∞)). So the text's construction is valid as B states it: the refinement has a new index set Λ with τ : Λ → I, not the cover's own index set (impossible in general, as the project notes). B => A is partly vacuous: conjuncts 3 and 4 come from B's (i) (Urysohn from a partition of unity subordinate to {X∖s, X∖t}), but conjuncts 1 and 2 are auxiliary chart lemmas B says nothing about, re-proved by copying the project's short arguments. So 'equivalent' means: same theorem (i), and B's extra construction follows from A's lemmas.
